title: Quant profile orchestration and smoke/regression test for INT8 weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Integrate INT8 weight-only quantization profiles produced by GPTQ and AWQ into Redwood's CI/regression harness and add a lightweight calibration workflow that can be executed in both hosted and dedicated environments. Deliverables: 1) an orchestration layer to schedule profile generation jobs, persist profiles to the artifact registry, and publish metadata (profile_id, model_version, quantizer, calibration_stats); 2) a reproducible calibration pipeline that supports per-shard and per-layer calibration sampling for AWQ; 3) a smoke/regression test suite that runs nightly and on PRs for model-serving changes; 4) accuracy validation scorecard with fail/pass thresholds and auto-notifications to the owner team.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestration: New quant-profile job type available in CI that can be triggered manually and scheduled nightly
Artifacts: Quant profiles stored in artifact registry with immutable profile_id and metadata tags (quantizer: gptq|awq, dtype: int8, shards: n)
Calibration: Pipeline produces calibration summary (per-layer scales, outlier counts, sample distribution) and a reproducible seed for each run

Regression tests: Nightly run produces a scorecard with at least 10 golden prompts per domain and aggregated delta metrics (PPL, ROUGE-like similarity, mean token-level deviation). Failures open a Linear issue and mark the PR as blocked if delta exceeds threshold
Smoke: Lightweight inference smoke test using quant profile to verify payload path, KV cache stability, and no runtime OOM on target instance types
Metrics: Introduce a quantitative threshold (e.g., median response delta <= 1.5% and 95th percentile hallucination score stable) and dashboard to track historical regressions
Integrations: PR hooking implemented (GitHub GH#1289) and a Confluence doc describing calibration knobs and guidance
tasks: Design quant-profile manifest format and metadata fields (profile_id, base_model, quantizer, shards, created_by, calibration_seed)
Extend CI to support a new job runner for quant-profile generation (container image with GPTQ/AWQ libs)
Implement calibration sampler that supports domain-stratified sampling and simulated drift datasets
Build a validator that replays golden prompt sets and computes the accuracy scorecard
Persist profile artifacts to S3-backed registry and expose read-only URL for runtime tests
Add nightly schedule and PR gating for critical runtime changes that can affect quantized outputs
Create alerts and automatic issue creation on large drifts with links to failing prompts and sample deltas
decisions_and_tradeoffs: We will keep GPTQ and AWQ pipelines separate executors to allow independent tuning and faster rollback. This adds duplication but reduces risk of cross-contamination.
Calibration sampling will prefer stratified domain samples over purely random draws to ensure coverage of worst-case tokens (trading off some average-case representativeness for tail safety).
We will store only the lightweight profile metadata in the console index and keep full calibration artifacts in the artifact registry to limit console storage costs.
For initial rollout we will run smoke/regtest on a smaller dedicated pool (n1-standard) rather than full-prod GPUs to limit cost; nightly full-GPU runs will be scheduled during off-peak hours.
risks: False negatives in regression: small but meaningful semantic regressions may not be captured by current automatic metrics
Artifact drift: quant profiles created with a different environment (kernel/cuda/cuDNN) could behave differently in production
Runtime incompatibility: AWQ per-shard profiles could expose bugs in our kernel selection path leading to OOMs or degraded latency
Cost: nightly full-GPU calibration and regression runs can increase monthly infra spend if not throttled
notes: Prototype PR: GH#1289 (wip) contains dockerfile and initial sampler from dataset team
Dashboard prototype: internal dashboard at /dashboards/quant_profiles/regression (read-only link)
Related ticket: ENG-8637 and ENG-9012 are historical references for quant-profile CI guardrails; this ticket aims for a different orchestration shape and nightly scorecarding
